newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican troops sweep rebel zones, detain three.
newsitem.headline: Mexican troops sweep rebel zones, detain three.

text.p: Mexican troops and police launched a counter-insurgency sweep in rebel zones of the southern state of Oaxaca, arresting three men, authorities said on Wednesday.

Oaxaca's state government said the operation was carried out on Tuesday in the coastal communities of San Francisco y Magdalena, Loxicha and Pochutla, some 350 miles (560 km) south-east of Mexico City.
The towns are in the heart of one of the regions where the Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR), a new Marxist guerrilla group, launched attacks on military and police bases two months ago.

Three weapons and 34 rounds of ammunition were confiscated in the sweep, which the state government said would continue. "Operations will continue in the zone with the goal of executing arrest orders," it said in a statement.

Those detained were Macedonio Jose Martinez, wanted for alleged murder, Nicolas Lorenzo Sebastian or Sebastian Nicolas Lorenzo, and Mario Ambrosio Martinez, both arrested for possession of unlicensed firearms.
Soldiers and police have now detained at least four dozen alleged members of the EPR group in operations since the rebels first appeared in Guerrero state on June 28.
The guerrillas, who have no links to the Zapatista rebels in the southern state of Chiapas, are currently holding to a self-declared ceasefire that ends October 27.
EPR rebels unilaterally declared September 25 they would not carry out offensives against the police or military to avoid disrupting local elections in Guerrero state, which were held on October 6.
